photos.c: 1924 CAN YOU NAME THE BLANKS? Standing: (Left to Right) Charlie Bain, ------, Wally Bayliss, Ken O'Kell, A.E.Smith, Mick Pyer, ------,H. J. Coxhead,Bert Footer, Syd King, Harry Parker Seated:(Left to Right) ------, ------, F. L. Buckingham,Frank Thomson,Harry 'Spider' Bruce,Jimmy Flatt, Arthur Lamm, ------,------.

This is thought to be the start of the Club '10' of 1926. Of the 11 starters, 9 finished. Winner was the smartly turned-out Bert Footer. (3rd from right) alongside of whom is the bespectacled Wally Bayliss who was to become our President, but probably retired from this race. Runner up to Footer was Micky Pyer (extreme left) who won in 1923 and 1924; with George Still (extreme right) 3rd. A.E. Smith (second from left) was 5th and J.G. Flatt (fourth from left) 6th.

Micky Pyer (extreme left) lines up at the start of the Belgrave 10 mile C.C. Championship in 1926. Having won the title in 1923 and 1924, this time he had to give way to his captain Bert Footer.
Left to right: A.D.Pyer, A.E.Smith, -, J.G.Flatt, -, -, -, -, H.E.Footer, W.L.Bayliss, G.Still.

photos.c: 1960 - John Merriman leads Gerry and Gordon Pirie in the National C.C.Champ. at West Bromwich. Basil Heatley was the winner and Gerry finished 4th.

"I DON'T WANT TO BE A BIG STAR, but I do want to be a bloody good actor. That's why I'm behaving like a lunatic." Hence this picture. Cantering in the background is Michael Crawford (soon to be seen with Barbra Streisand in the Hollywood version of "Hello Dolly") who has just been signed to appear in Michael Winner's next film, "The Games," based on the novel by Hugh Atkinson and researcher Phillip Knightley. "The Games" recounts the trials of four Olympic marathon runners and to ensure the authenticity of the athletics in his film, Winner has hired Gordon Pirie as his technical adviser. It is Pirie (see above) who leads Crawford on training sessions across Wimbledon Common. "My training might not make much difference to audience reaction," says Crawford, "but the extra muscle will make me feel it's right." Next part: "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner"
John Davies trains at the Duke of York's Barracks with Gordon Pirie (left) and Chris Chataway (behind). September 1956.

photos.c: Belgrave's 'winning team' of Hall, Piddington and Bonsor are pictured above--what prospects!.

FRONTISPIECE (Photo: Ed Lacey)--Who's that guy with George Piddington? Well, George condescendingly turned away his own autograph hunters to allow some Aussie fella called Ron Clarke to join him in a grin at Ed Lacey. They were front and back markers in a 1500 metres handicap at White City. We leave you to guess which was which!

The Belgrave 20 Mile Road Race. Centre: Graham Taylor (Camb H), the winner. Top left to right: Geoff Pearson, George Piddington, Alan Black and Trevor Hart. Bottom: John Davies, Bob Richardson and Charlie Henn.

George Piddington pictured during the Belgrave '20'. At this stage his antennae must have been malfunctioning for he does not seem to have detected 'the grey ghost', Hon. Treasurer John Baker, creeping up behind.

Opposite page. The Philips 100x1 mile relay. Top right: Charlie Gillett. Centre left to right: Dudley Gordon, Gerry Sexton, George Piddington and Robin Brown. Bottom left to right: Simon Pritchard, Joe McDonald and Alan Painter.

Left: Enjoying the occasion.  Pat Mead, Tony Binda, Marianne Black, Gerry North, Alan Black, the late Laurie O'Hara, George Piddington, Charlie Henn, Ted Pallant, Chris Steer, Charlie Manning.

Sadly this was the last time that we saw Laurie O'Hara.  He died the following day while out running.

Above:  At the White City Stadium, in 1968,  the Fire Brigade Sports 1500 metres handicap brought together the then world record holder Ron Clarke of Australia … and George Piddington of Belgrave Harriers. We’ll leave you to decided which one was the front marker and which one was off “scratch”.

Part of the Belgrave coaching course 1965
Amongst those standing are Ben Lulham (far left), George Piddington (4th from left), Frank Simmons (6th from left) Jack Hampshire Snr and Charlie Jones (both partly hidden) and Tom Carter (far right).

photos.c: BOTTOM LEFT: Ted Pallant.
September 21st 1963 and Ted strides out in the Polytechnic Road Relay at Chiswick.

Left: Nearly two miles gone in the '5¾'. It's September 1966 and among the 39 competitors in the race, this bunch are out to settle personal scores - or perhaps just enjoy the sunshine. The runners are: Financial wizards Keith Miller (106) and Jim Heathfield (93), Ted Pallant (94), talented youth and junior Tony Brooks (37) - lost to the sport before making impact as a senior, Dave McMillan (12) - now fighting back from terrible injuries sustained while out training and hit by a car, P.Blair-Fish (46).

The traditional team photo before the start of the first Surrey League Race. Back row - Bruce Barton, Geremew Wolde, Rex Bale, Mike Webb, Don Anderson, Gerry Adams, Darryl Ochse, Alasdair McLean Foreman, Roger Alsop, Adam Cowmeadow, Tony Barden, Kevin Quinn, Pete Gilbey, Harry Corbett, Erwenn Lemenager, Rob Harding, Andy Brown, Ted Pallant. Front row: Rob McHarg, Steve Clarke, Will Cockerell, Eric Hall (President), Junior Galley, Jamie Kirton, Elvis Rimdap, Roy Collier, Aldis Ulrych.

Left: Getting ready for the "off" at Brockwell Park. Stuart Paton, Ted Pallant (President), Alex Luce, Rob Harding, Marlon Anderson (obscured), Steve Hewes, Said Chettati, Gerry Adams, Charlie Dickinson, Mike Nouch, Jim Estall, Derek Manning (behind), Tony Binda, Roger Alsop, Mick Graham (behind), Matt Yates, Alan Mead, Bruce Barton (behind), Bill Bull.
Left:  Ted Pallant, President, congratulates Past President Bill Lucas on his achievements.

Left: Enjoying the occasion.  Pat Mead, Tony Binda, Marianne Black, Gerry North, Alan Black, the late Laurie O'Hara, George Piddington, Charlie Henn, Ted Pallant, Chris Steer, Charlie Manning.

Sadly this was the last time that we saw Laurie O'Hara.  He died the following day while out running.
Below:  Snowy Brooks, Ted Pallant and Sheila, Bill Lucas and Sheena enjoy the festivities at Belgrave Hall on April 19th.
Above: Ted Pallant and Denis Brickwood recall old days and enjoy the 'spread'.
